entries.name: auto-editor
entries.use_for: Automatically cut silence and dead air from videos and export to editors or rendered files.
entries.why: Popular, actively maintained CLI for automated rough cuts; exports to Premiere, Resolve and FCP.

entries.name: FastVideo
entries.use_for: Speed up inference and post-training of open video diffusion models like Wan and Hunyuan.
entries.why: Unified, actively developed framework for accelerated video generation; Apache-2.0.

entries.name: FFmpeg
entries.use_for: Decode, encode, transcode, mux and filter almost any audio/video format from the CLI or libav* libraries.
entries.why: The de facto media processing engine underneath most video tools; LGPL-2.1+ by default (verified LICENSE.md).

entries.name: FFmpeg-Builds
entries.use_for: Download up-to-date static/shared FFmpeg builds for Windows and Linux in CI or apps
entries.why: Widely used source of nightly and release FFmpeg binaries (GPL/LGPL variants) built reproducibly via GitHub Actions.

entries.name: ffmpeg.wasm
entries.use_for: Run FFmpeg in the browser or Node via WebAssembly for client-side video conversion.
entries.why: Most widely used WASM port of FFmpeg; avoids a server for trimming, converting and thumbnailing.

entries.name: go2rtc
entries.use_for: Restream and convert camera streams between RTSP, WebRTC, HLS, MSE and more.
entries.why: Zero-dependency streaming server widely used with Frigate/Home Assistant for low-latency camera video.

entries.name: GStreamer
entries.use_for: Pipeline-based multimedia framework for building capture, transcoding, streaming and playback apps
entries.why: The standard plugin-based media pipeline framework on Linux and embedded devices; bindings for Rust, Python and more

license_verified.note: LICENSE is LGPL 2.1; some optional plugins with GPL deps are opt-in

entries.name: GSYVideoPlayer
entries.use_for: Add a full-featured video player to an Android app
entries.why: Wraps IJKPlayer, ExoPlayer and MediaPlayer behind one API with caching, danmaku, filters and fullscreen handling.

entries.name: hls.js
entries.use_for: Play HLS (m3u8) streams in browsers that lack native HLS via Media Source Extensions.
entries.why: The standard HLS playback library on the web, used by most JS video players.

entries.name: HyperFrames
entries.use_for: Author videos as HTML/CSS/JS compositions and render them deterministically to MP4.
entries.why: Apache-2.0 HTML-to-video renderer designed for coding agents; a permissive alternative to Remotion-style workflows.

entries.name: LivePortrait
entries.use_for: Animate a still portrait from a driving video or expressions
entries.why: Efficient Kuaishou/Kling portrait animation model with stitching and retargeting control; MIT-licensed code.

entries.name: Mediabunny
entries.use_for: Read, write and convert MP4/WebM/MP3 and more in the browser with WebCodecs, no FFmpeg needed
entries.why: Pure-TypeScript media toolkit (successor to mp4-muxer/webm-muxer) for fast in-browser transcoding, trimming and muxing

entries.name: MediaMTX
entries.use_for: Ready-to-use media server and proxy to read, publish and route live video over RTSP, RTMP, WebRTC, HLS and SRT
entries.why: Single binary that converts between all common live-streaming protocols; the default self-hosted relay for cameras and live video

entries.name: Motion Canvas
entries.use_for: Create animated explainer videos programmatically with TypeScript and a live-preview editor
entries.why: MIT-licensed code-to-video tool with a timeline editor; a fully open alternative for programmatic motion graphics

entries.name: MoviePy
entries.use_for: Script video edits in Python: cut, concatenate, add titles, overlays and effects.
entries.why: Long-standing, simple Python API for programmatic editing; MIT licensed and actively maintained.

entries.name: mpv
entries.use_for: Embed a capable video player in your app via libmpv, or script playback from the CLI
entries.why: libmpv powers many desktop players; plays nearly any format with GPU rendering and a Lua/JS scripting API.

license_verified.note: Copyright file: GPLv2+ by default, LGPLv2.1+ when built with -Dgpl=false

entries.name: OpenTimelineIO
entries.use_for: Read, write and convert editorial timelines between NLEs (EDL, FCP XML and more via adapters).
entries.why: ASWF industry-standard API and format for editorial timeline interchange.

entries.name: PyAV
entries.use_for: Pythonic bindings to FFmpeg libraries for frame-level decoding, encoding and muxing
entries.why: Direct access to FFmpeg packets and frames from Python without shelling out; used by torchvision, auto-editor and many ML pipelines

entries.name: Shaka Player
entries.use_for: Adaptive DASH and HLS playback in the browser with DRM, offline storage and captions
entries.why: Google-backed player library for adaptive streaming with Widevine/PlayReady DRM; the go-to when hls.js alone isn't enough

entries.name: video-use
entries.use_for: Let a coding agent edit videos (cuts, captions, overlays) from natural language
entries.why: From the browser-use team: gives Claude Code/Codex a toolkit to transcribe, cut and render edits programmatically.

entries.name: Video.js
entries.use_for: Embed a customizable, skinnable HTML5 video player with HLS/DASH support and plugins.
entries.why: Mature open-source web player with a large plugin ecosystem; Apache-2.0.

entries.name: Vidstack Player
entries.use_for: Accessible, customisable audio/video player components for React and web components
entries.why: Modern successor to Plyr/Vime: headless-friendly player UI with HLS, YouTube and Vimeo providers built in

entries.name: Wan 2.2
entries.use_for: Generate videos from text or images with open-weight diffusion models you can self-host.
entries.why: Leading open-weight video generation model family under Apache-2.0.

entries.name: yt-dlp
entries.use_for: Download video and audio from YouTube and thousands of other sites from the CLI or Python.
entries.why: The maintained youtube-dl successor with the broadest site coverage; embeddable as a Python module.
